title: What today cost, and what that says

text:
Five workers landed today for **$23.29**, all Sonnet at the same effort — so the spread is the work, not the model.

| task | cost | turns | rework |
|---|---|---|---|
| live-select | $7.77 | 128 | yes |
| safe-rollout | $7.45 | 139 | yes |
| head-mobile | $3.86 | 103 | none |
| v3-ways-out | $2.55 | 69 | none |
| traps-consolidate | $1.66 | 49 | none |

## Cost tracks how WIDE the brief was — and so does rework

The two expensive ones are the two briefs that carried several items: safe-rollout had three fixes, live-select had four. They are also **the only two that needed fixing at harvest**.

The three single-purpose briefs cost $1.66–$3.86 and landed clean.

A four-item brief is not four times the work. It is about three times the cost *and* the source of the errors.

## Why I was writing wide briefs

Your dictations arrive with four things in them. I was passing that straight through to the minion — but **your message shape is not the unit of work**, and treating it as one is my mistake, not yours.

From here a brief carries one deliverable unless two are genuinely inseparable. The alternative I considered and rejected: keep wide briefs and add a critic pass, which pays twice for the same defect.

## A second cost, and it is yours to unlock

Those turn counts are inflated by refused commands — safe-rollout took **139 turns to write four files**, most of it retrying `node`, `git` and `node --check` before giving up.

The missing Bash permission rule is not only costing proof quality. It is costing money.
